sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle for direct bachelor's-to-PhD admission once the UChicago bachelor's is completed before
enrollment; F-1 applicants apply as international. MSCS expects a related undergraduate degree, GPA at least
3.0 in the final 60 semester/90 quarter hours and in mathematics beyond calculus. Pure mathematics
preparation includes linear algebra, abstract algebra and a year of analysis. These are minimum qualifications,
not an admission prediction. [s2] [s3] [s4] [s6] [s8]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose the Mathematics PhD, arrange three academic referees, upload records and the personal statement,
and pay or obtain an authorized fee waiver. International applicants must have all supporting items received
by the program deadline. Supervisor consent is not listed as an admission prerequisite. Visa/financial
certification is an after-admission step. Ask the department early about University Fellowship nomination and
its internal deadline. [s2] [s6] [s7] [s14]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No supervisor commitment is required publicly. Schaposnik explicitly invites prospective students interested in
her geometry group to contact schapos@uic.edu and offers application guidance; this is a standing invitation,
not a guarantee of 2027 capacity. Other faculty availability should be asked individually. Department
admissions questions belong with the graduate program, not a request for faculty to pre-adjudicate an
application. [s2] [s5] [s43]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use UIC's graduate application and monitor its status checklist. The central process accepts electronic
PDF/Word documents and generally discards unsolicited paper materials; follow program-specific formats if
present. Requests for financial/visa documents occur after admission. Do not reuse another program's or prior
year's uploaded materials without authorization. [s6] [s7] [s8] [s9]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Fall 2027 applications are centrally available, but MSCS publishes a standing December 15 deadline rather
than a fully dated Fall 2027 page. Fellowship 2027 competition opens December 1; retained nomination

deadlines and assistantship dollar figures are older/current-2026-27 evidence. Recheck the portal and
fellowship page when the competition opens. [s1] [s14] [s45] [s47]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Standing rule]
December 15, annual standing deadline for fall PhD entry; the department does not attach an explicit 2027
year, submission hour or timezone. Fall 2027 applications are available centrally. Confirm December 15, 2026
and the portal cutoff rather than treating that inferred date as a published cycle-specific deadline. [s1] [s3] [s47]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
Ordinary assistantship consideration is automatic for complete applications by the admission deadline.
University/Access Fellowship 2027 competition is announced to open December 1; the retained February 2,
2026, 4 p.m. Central nomination deadline belongs to the prior competition. The 2027 university and earlier
MSCS nomination deadlines are unresolved. [s13] [s14] [s15] [s45]
Reference receipt [Standing rule]
International admissions requires supporting documents by the published program deadline, so plan for all
three letters by December 15. No separate guaranteed letter grace period or cycle-specific hour/timezone was
found. Do not rely on the ability to upload after submitting the application as permission to submit late. [s6] [s7]
[s9]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
When required, official scores must arrive with the complete application by the program deadline; ETS
reporting may take about two weeks. Scores must be within two years at application. ETS institutional code
1851. GRE scores are optional; ask whether optional scores received late would be read. [s2] [s6]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
All international supporting documents are due at the program's deadline; there is no second document
deadline promised. The portal permits later uploads after initial application submission, which does not
override that deadline. Final official credentials are required after admission as instructed. [s6] [s7] [s8]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
UIC explicitly states that funded applicants have until April 15 to accept financial-support offers for the coming
academic year. This is a standing policy, not an individually dated 2027 offer. Verify the actual offer deadline.
The linked UIC release-after-April-15 language may predate current CGS rules; consult the report's shared CGS
discussion. [s17] [s45]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Math PhD catalog: TOEFL new scale overall 5, Reading 4, Listening 4, Speaking 5, Writing 4.5; old scale overall
100, R19/L17/S23/W21. IELTS overall 7 and each component 7; PTE overall 68, R66/L66/S68/W66. MSCS's
general page instead gives lower speaking thresholds (TOEFL 4.5 or old 20; PTE 66), creating a conflict: use the
PhD-specific threshold pending clarification. Central Duolingo acceptance begins Fall 2027 (130, each 125), but
MSCS acceptance is not established. International TAs have additional assessment/orientation. [s3] [s4] [s5] [s6]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A UChicago student with two years of full-time academic study in the United States within the preceding five
years can satisfy UIC's admission-test exemption once transcripts are evaluated; degree completion is not
stated as necessary for this route. English-medium instruction alone elsewhere is insufficient. This admission
exemption does not remove the international-TA spoken-English assessment/orientation. Request confirmation
if the portal still lists a test. [s5] [s6]

GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional; MSCS says applicants are not penalized for omitting the GRE. No numerical minimum published. [s2]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional; the same no-penalty policy covers the Mathematics Subject GRE. No score cutoff published. [s2]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three academic letters are required for the Mathematics PhD. The general graduate-school minimum does not
reduce the department's requirement. [s2] [s4]
Scholarship references [Standing rule]
University Fellowship nomination reuses the three admission letters and adds a department nomination letter
plus financial-support/transmittal paperwork. No fourth external referee is specified. The applicant does not
self-submit the university nomination. PIF uses the fellowship nomination and may need a one-page
faculty-career statement; no separate external referee found. [s14] [s16]
What sends the invitation [Unresolved]
UIC says providing referee email information prompts the electronic reference request and requests are
initiated through the application/checklist. The public instructions do not unambiguously identify the exact
Save/Send button or establish whether simply typing an address immediately emails the referee. Confirm the
portal wording before entering details. [s7] [s8] [s9]
Before versus after submission [Unresolved]
No public evidence establishes that invitations wait until final application submission. UIC allows an application
to be submitted before all supplemental items are received. Request letters early using the portal's explicit
request control; do not assume final submission is necessary. [s7] [s8]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
The application-status checklist displays materials received and receipt dates; applicants may receive weekly
missing-item emails. Contact Admissions for technical problems with reference invitations and the department
for substantive requirements. [s8] [s9]
Updating and reusing letters [Unresolved]
Applicants who previously applied but did not enroll must submit materials again; materials are not
automatically transferred to a future application or another program. The public pages do not establish

whether a submitted letter can be replaced within the same application; ask MSCS/Admissions. Fellowship
nomination can reuse the current admission letters. [s6] [s8] [s14]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
The published August 2026-May 2027 minimum for a 50% nine-month appointment is USD 25,652, with full
tuition and partial fee waivers; this is a university floor/current appointment basis, not a confirmed Fall 2027
math offer or 12-month stipend. Summer support and exact health-insurance residual cost are unverified.
University Fellowship currently pays USD 33,000 over 12 months (USD 2,750/month), with tuition and specified
partial fee/health support. [s13] [s14] [s46]
Years of support [Standing rule]
MSCS says almost all PhD students receive support and good-standing students normally retain it through their
degree; no unconditional fixed six-year entry guarantee was located. University Fellowship supports year one
and a second fellowship year after prelims, no earlier than year four and no later than year five; department
funding covers years two and three at a minimum nine-month 50% appointment. Summer top-offs in those
departmental years are no longer part of that fellowship rule. [s12] [s13] [s14]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Department assistantships are open to eligible international students subject to lawful employment and TA
language clearance. University Fellowship explicitly has no citizenship restriction. Access Fellowship requires
US citizenship/permanent residency or qualifying Illinois RISE eligibility and therefore is not an ordinary F-1
option. PIF may be accessed through University Fellowship nomination; confirm its individual eligibility. [s13]
[s14] [s15] [s16] [s46]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Appointments are competitive and require academic progress and satisfactory duties. A 50% appointment is
normally 20 hours/week; international students face term-time employment limits. Continuing MSCS students
submit annual academic assessment and teaching availability. Typical TA registration is 12 credits; University
Fellowship requires nine credits fall/spring and, if summer enrollment is undertaken, three to five. Exact
benefits and summer availability must appear in the offer. [s12] [s13] [s14] [s46]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
All complete applicants receive ordinary funding consideration without a separate initial assistantship
application. University Fellowship requires department nomination; the applicant cannot self-nominate. The
page currently limits each program to two nominees, at most one external applicant (John is external); verify
the 2027 rules on opening. PIF nomination is also departmental. [s13] [s14] [s16]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Research assistantships, department teaching assistantships, merit-based Board of Trustees tuition waivers
and Graduate College fellowships are distinct routes. A tuition waiver alone has no stipend. PIF currently
provides three USD 33,000 fellowship years and one USD 10,000 supplement to a teaching/research
appointment. Eligibility, nomination and benefit details must be checked individually; no blanket eligibility is
inferred for external scholarships. [s12] [s16]
Application fee [Conflict]
USD 80 application fee, effective Fall 2026. A further USD 100 credential-evaluation fee applies to applicants
with postsecondary coursework outside the United States, not simply to all foreign citizens. A UChicago-only
academic history should avoid that extra fee; confirm any overseas study/transfer record. The MSCS FAQ's USD
70 fee is outdated. [s5] [s6]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Central Admissions does not grant financial-hardship waivers or defer payment. Listed categories include
qualifying UIC alumni/current students, specified UI-system graduate students/employees, McNair and certain

Illinois veterans; UChicago is not the University of Illinois. Graduate College research-engagement waivers
exclude ordinary international applicants. A department may elect to pay an applicant's fee, but no MSCS
promise was found; inquire before paying. [s10] [s11]

University of Illinois Chicago
United States · Mathematics PhD
Rank verified separately
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• A standing December 15 date is not explicit Fall 2027 confirmation.
• Use current central fees and PhD-specific English requirements; departmental pages conflict.
• University Fellowship is internationally eligible but department-nominated; 2027 competition details are not
yet all published.
• USD 25,652 is a nine-month 2026-27 minimum, not a 2027 annual offer.
• Faculty list is a research-fit shortlist of current faculty; research-rank supervision needs checking. Emeriti
including Gillet, Libgober and Stephen Yau are not represented as ordinary incoming advisers. Benjamin
Bakker is now at UChicago.
Eligibility and preparation
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Eligible in principle for direct bachelor's-to-PhD admission once the UChicago bachelor's is completed before
enrollment; F-1 applicants apply as international. MSCS expects a related undergraduate degree, GPA at least
3.0 in the final 60 semester/90 quarter hours and in mathematics beyond calculus. Pure mathematics
preparation includes linear algebra, abstract algebra and a year of analysis. These are minimum qualifications,
not an admission prediction. [s2] [s3] [s4] [s6] [s8]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Choose the Mathematics PhD, arrange three academic referees, upload records and the personal statement,
and pay or obtain an authorized fee waiver. International applicants must have all supporting items received
by the program deadline. Supervisor consent is not listed as an admission prerequisite. Visa/financial
certification is an after-admission step. Ask the department early about University Fellowship nomination and
its internal deadline. [s2] [s6] [s7] [s14]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No supervisor commitment is required publicly. Schaposnik explicitly invites prospective students interested in
her geometry group to contact schapos@uic.edu and offers application guidance; this is a standing invitation,
not a guarantee of 2027 capacity. Other faculty availability should be asked individually. Department
admissions questions belong with the graduate program, not a request for faculty to pre-adjudicate an
application. [s2] [s5] [s43]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
Use UIC's graduate application and monitor its status checklist. The central process accepts electronic
PDF/Word documents and generally discards unsolicited paper materials; follow program-specific formats if
present. Requests for financial/visa documents occur after admission. Do not reuse another program's or prior
year's uploaded materials without authorization. [s6] [s7] [s8] [s9]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Fall 2027 applications are centrally available, but MSCS publishes a standing December 15 deadline rather
than a fully dated Fall 2027 page. Fellowship 2027 competition opens December 1; retained nomination

deadlines and assistantship dollar figures are older/current-2026-27 evidence. Recheck the portal and
fellowship page when the competition opens. [s1] [s14] [s45] [s47]
Deadlines by stage
Academic application [Standing rule]
December 15, annual standing deadline for fall PhD entry; the department does not attach an explicit 2027
year, submission hour or timezone. Fall 2027 applications are available centrally. Confirm December 15, 2026
and the portal cutoff rather than treating that inferred date as a published cycle-specific deadline. [s1] [s3] [s47]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
Ordinary assistantship consideration is automatic for complete applications by the admission deadline.
University/Access Fellowship 2027 competition is announced to open December 1; the retained February 2,
2026, 4 p.m. Central nomination deadline belongs to the prior competition. The 2027 university and earlier
MSCS nomination deadlines are unresolved. [s13] [s14] [s15] [s45]
Reference receipt [Standing rule]
International admissions requires supporting documents by the published program deadline, so plan for all
three letters by December 15. No separate guaranteed letter grace period or cycle-specific hour/timezone was
found. Do not rely on the ability to upload after submitting the application as permission to submit late. [s6] [s7]
[s9]
Test-score receipt [Standing rule]
When required, official scores must arrive with the complete application by the program deadline; ETS
reporting may take about two weeks. Scores must be within two years at application. ETS institutional code
1851. GRE scores are optional; ask whether optional scores received late would be read. [s2] [s6]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
All international supporting documents are due at the program's deadline; there is no second document
deadline promised. The portal permits later uploads after initial application submission, which does not
override that deadline. Final official credentials are required after admission as instructed. [s6] [s7] [s8]
Accepting an offer [Standing rule]
UIC explicitly states that funded applicants have until April 15 to accept financial-support offers for the coming
academic year. This is a standing policy, not an individually dated 2027 offer. Verify the actual offer deadline.
The linked UIC release-after-April-15 language may predate current CGS rules; consult the report's shared CGS
discussion. [s17] [s45]
English and GRE
English requirement [Conflict]
Math PhD catalog: TOEFL new scale overall 5, Reading 4, Listening 4, Speaking 5, Writing 4.5; old scale overall
100, R19/L17/S23/W21. IELTS overall 7 and each component 7; PTE overall 68, R66/L66/S68/W66. MSCS's
general page instead gives lower speaking thresholds (TOEFL 4.5 or old 20; PTE 66), creating a conflict: use the
PhD-specific threshold pending clarification. Central Duolingo acceptance begins Fall 2027 (130, each 125), but
MSCS acceptance is not established. International TAs have additional assessment/orientation. [s3] [s4] [s5] [s6]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A UChicago student with two years of full-time academic study in the United States within the preceding five

Funding and fees
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
The published August 2026-May 2027 minimum for a 50% nine-month appointment is USD 25,652, with full
tuition and partial fee waivers; this is a university floor/current appointment basis, not a confirmed Fall 2027
math offer or 12-month stipend. Summer support and exact health-insurance residual cost are unverified.
University Fellowship currently pays USD 33,000 over 12 months (USD 2,750/month), with tuition and specified
partial fee/health support. [s13] [s14] [s46]
Years of support [Standing rule]
MSCS says almost all PhD students receive support and good-standing students normally retain it through their
degree; no unconditional fixed six-year entry guarantee was located. University Fellowship supports year one
and a second fellowship year after prelims, no earlier than year four and no later than year five; department
funding covers years two and three at a minimum nine-month 50% appointment. Summer top-offs in those
departmental years are no longer part of that fellowship rule. [s12] [s13] [s14]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
Department assistantships are open to eligible international students subject to lawful employment and TA
language clearance. University Fellowship explicitly has no citizenship restriction. Access Fellowship requires
US citizenship/permanent residency or qualifying Illinois RISE eligibility and therefore is not an ordinary F-1
option. PIF may be accessed through University Fellowship nomination; confirm its individual eligibility. [s13]
[s14] [s15] [s16] [s46]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Appointments are competitive and require academic progress and satisfactory duties. A 50% appointment is
normally 20 hours/week; international students face term-time employment limits. Continuing MSCS students
submit annual academic assessment and teaching availability. Typical TA registration is 12 credits; University
Fellowship requires nine credits fall/spring and, if summer enrollment is undertaken, three to five. Exact
benefits and summer availability must appear in the offer. [s12] [s13] [s14] [s46]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
All complete applicants receive ordinary funding consideration without a separate initial assistantship
application. University Fellowship requires department nomination; the applicant cannot self-nominate. The
page currently limits each program to two nominees, at most one external applicant (John is external); verify
the 2027 rules on opening. PIF nomination is also departmental. [s13] [s14] [s16]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Research assistantships, department teaching assistantships, merit-based Board of Trustees tuition waivers
and Graduate College fellowships are distinct routes. A tuition waiver alone has no stipend. PIF currently
provides three USD 33,000 fellowship years and one USD 10,000 supplement to a teaching/research
appointment. Eligibility, nomination and benefit details must be checked individually; no blanket eligibility is
inferred for external scholarships. [s12] [s16]

USD 80 application fee, effective Fall 2026. A further USD 100 credential-evaluation fee applies to applicants
with postsecondary coursework outside the United States, not simply to all foreign citizens. A UChicago-only
academic history should avoid that extra fee; confirm any overseas study/transfer record. The MSCS FAQ's USD
70 fee is outdated. [s5] [s6]

exclude ordinary international applicants. A department may elect to pay an applicant's fee, but no MSCS
